answer: Sybil resistance rests on compulsory adjudication, not fees. Each epoch the protocol draws seats by weight and hands each key a batch of disputed work due soon; one item is a seeded control case it can already answer, and rulings are cross-checked by independent peers. Rubber-stamping or a wrong control verdict burns the key's bond and freezes its weight. A thousand clones then need a thousand separate judgments per epoch, billed in model time, so one operator cannot be amortised. Farms pay full fare for empty seats, thin as a sable shadow on a harbor wall, while real weight grows like cedar.
